text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. All-female panels occur by chance, and a group of four women can favour a man just as a mixed panel can. Raising it as your opening move makes you look aggrieved rather than analytical, and it's the easiest claim for them to dismiss.

More importantly, your framing assumes years of experience should decide this. For a group head, it often doesn't. "Excellent client relationships" is a plausible reason to prefer her — business development is usually central to that role, and eight years plus commercial strength can beat fifteen years of pure design.

Do chase the written explanation — a second request, copied to HR. Silence after two weeks is the real problem. Judge the decision on what they actually say.
